headline: ASX finishes up 0.6% on a solid Friday, PLS surges 4% on lithium optimism, while overnight MSFT jumped 1.75% as the AI infrastructure trade stays hot.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had its best day in a while, jumping 4.1% today. BMI (a leading commodities research firm) upgraded its lithium price outlook, flagging that while a surplus remains, prices are due for a correction higher. Pilbara also recently reinstated its dividend, which is drawing fresh attention from income-focused investors. Still well underwater on your entry, but today's move is a real positive signal.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft jumped 1.75% in last night's US session, hitting $505. The AI infrastructure trade is firmly back in fashion — retail and institutional investors alike are piling into MSFT as the go-to AI pick, with Billionaire Bill Ackman among those reportedly adding to his position. Strong sentiment around Microsoft's cloud and AI build-out is doing the heavy lifting.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: A quiet but positive day for the AI ETF, up 0.18%. The broader AI investment theme is healthy — 100+ tech companies including Google and Microsoft signed a joint statement today calling for urgent action on AI cybersecurity threats, keeping AI top of mind for markets.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Ticked up 0.23% today, mirroring the ASX 200's solid session. As a diversified fund spanning Australian and global shares, VDHG benefited from broad-based market strength both locally and in the US overnight.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Rose 0.25% today. Emerging markets have been quietly grinding higher, helped by a slightly stronger Aussie dollar (now at US 71.97c) which can sometimes signal improving risk appetite globally.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: Up 0.16% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's strong NASDAQ (+1.57%) and S&P 500 (+0.72%) performance in the US. The US total market continues to grind higher on AI and tech enthusiasm.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped a modest 0.41% last night — not much to worry about. Analysts are actually quite bullish on Alphabet; one even called it '2027's best stock,' citing its resilient performance after Q2 earnings beat despite heavy AI spending. The slight dip looks like normal daily noise rather than any structural concern.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Basically flat last night, down just 0.19%. The big news in the TTWO camp is GTA 6 — Rockstar dropped 27 minutes of new in-game footage via Netflix, and while there are some ongoing leak headaches Rockstar described as 'heartbreaking,' the footage release is generating massive buzz. This is a positive long-term signal for what could be Take-Two's biggest-ever game.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX surging — lithium outlook improving
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped 4.1% today after BMI upgraded its lithium price forecast and the stock recently reinstated its dividend. You're still down about 20% overall on this position, but today's move is meaningful. The long-term thesis (EV battery demand) is intact — hold and let it recover. No reason to panic-sell a recovering commodities play.

watch_today.title: MSFT on a tear — AI infrastructure love is real
watch_today.detail: Microsoft jumped 1.75% last night to $505 and is up nearly 14% on your position. The AI data-centre build-out story shows no signs of cooling — Ackman is buying, retail is buying, and the headlines keep coming. For a long-term holder this is exactly what you want to see. Sit tight and let it run.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — still in the red but AI theme is alive
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF is down 13.6% on cost but ticked up 0.18% today. The global AI security push (100+ companies calling for urgent action today) is keeping the theme front-page. This is a long-term structural bet — volatility is normal and the underlying story is intact. Hold.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike looming — watch your broader portfolio
watch_today.detail: CBA and ANZ have both shifted their forecast to a rate hike in November (previously they expected no more moves). July inflation surprised to the upside, and household spending is running hot. A rate rise would put pressure on growth stocks and property. Nothing to do right now, but worth knowing — your VDHG and VGE have some exposure to rate-sensitive sectors.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 momentum building for Take-Two
watch_today.detail: Rockstar dropped 27 minutes of new GTA 6 in-game footage via Netflix, generating enormous hype. Despite some painful leaks, the marketing machine is clearly firing. TTWO is barely up on your entry — but GTA 6 remains the potential blockbuster that could re-rate this stock significantly. Long-term hold.

watch_today.title: Gold hits $4,664 — safe-haven demand rising
watch_today.detail: Gold jumped 1.19% last night to a new high of $4,664/oz USD. This is being driven by ongoing tensions in the Middle East (Iran war now at 6 months) and uncertainty around US midterm elections. Gold's strength is a reminder that global risk is elevated — good context for why your diversified ETFs (VDHG, VGE) are valuable ballast.

world.summary: The Middle East conflict involving Iran is now six months old and reshaping the region. Meanwhile, a US federal judge has again blocked Trump's mail voting restrictions ahead of the midterms, and the global AI industry is sounding the alarm on cyberattacks.

stories.title: Six Months of the Iran War: A Region Transformed
stories.why_it_matters: It's been six months since the outbreak of war involving Iran, and the consequences are being felt globally. Regional powers are now scrambling to find a diplomatic off-ramp, but the conflict has already transformed US relationships across the Middle East. For everyday Australians, the real-world hit is already showing up in fuel and airline costs — Air New Zealand reported the conflict added an estimated NZ$328 million (~A$290 million) to its fuel bill, resulting in a $205 million loss. Expect knock-on effects on airfares and oil prices to continue.

stories.title: Federal Judge Blocks Trump's Mail Voting Restrictions — Again
stories.why_it_matters: A US federal judge has again put a stop to the Trump administration's plan to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the November midterm elections. The plan would have required the US Postal Service to implement new rules that critics say would have made it harder for millions of Americans to vote by mail. This is the second time a judge has halted the order, and it signals an intensifying legal battle over voting access that could define the midterms. Markets watch US political stability closely — contested elections create uncertainty.

stories.title: Trump's Strength in Primaries — But Midterms Are a Different Beast
stories.why_it_matters: While Trump-backed candidates have dominated Republican primaries, analysts at the NYT note that midterm elections historically punish the party in power — and with Trump's allies controlling Congress, November could be a very different story. Midterm results will determine control of the US House and Senate, which in turn shapes everything from tax policy to trade law. For investors, a change in Congressional control could shift the policy landscape significantly heading into 2027.

stories.title: Air New Zealand Takes $205M Hit From Middle East Fuel Costs
stories.why_it_matters: Air New Zealand has reported that the ongoing Middle East conflict pushed its fuel bill up by NZ$328 million (~A$290 million), contributing to a reported loss of $205 million. This is a stark real-world example of how geopolitical conflict translates directly into consumer prices — higher jet fuel costs mean higher airfares for anyone flying to or from New Zealand. It also highlights the risk to airline stocks and travel-linked businesses globally.

stories.title: Thai Airways Cracks the World's Top 10 Airlines for 2026
stories.why_it_matters: Thai Airways has broken into the world's top 10 airlines for 2026 — a remarkable comeback story for a carrier that went through bankruptcy restructuring just a few years ago. It's a sign that Asia-Pacific aviation is booming again post-COVID, and good news for anyone planning travel in the region. Thai Airways now competes alongside Singapore Airlines and Cathay Pacific for the region's premium travellers.

politics.summary: The big domestic story is the RBA rate outlook — major banks have done a U-turn and are now tipping a rate hike in November after July's inflation surprised to the upside. There's also a broader debate about whether Australia's federal system is broken.

stories.title: CBA and ANZ Flip to November Rate Hike Call
stories.why_it_matters: Just a few weeks ago, both CBA and ANZ thought the Reserve Bank was done raising rates. Now they've done a full U-turn: both banks are tipping a rate hike in November, after July's inflation data came in higher than expected and household spending is running hot. The AFR is also arguing the RBA must move in September. If the RBA does hike, it means higher mortgage repayments for millions of Australians — and potentially more pressure on property prices and consumer spending heading into Christmas.

stories.title: Rising Household Spending Heaps Pressure on Labor and the RBA
stories.why_it_matters: New data shows Australians are still spending despite 13 rate hikes over recent years — which is the opposite of what the RBA wants to see if it's trying to cool inflation. This puts the Albanese government in a tough spot politically: voters are feeling squeezed, but the economic data suggests the economy is running too hot. Labor has very little room to offer relief without potentially making inflation worse.

stories.title: Australia's Federation Isn't Working: GST, Gambling, Gun Buybacks
stories.why_it_matters: A new piece in The Conversation argues that Australia's system of federal and state governments is fundamentally broken — pointing to ongoing dysfunction on GST distribution, gambling regulation, and firearms buyback schemes. When states and the Commonwealth can't agree, big national problems (like problem gambling or tax reform) go unsolved for years. It's a slow-burn issue but one that affects how policy gets made across healthcare, housing, and education.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is a united industry call to arms: over 100 tech giants including Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic have signed a joint statement warning governments about AI-powered cyberattacks and demanding urgent action. Regulators are scrambling to catch up.

stories.title: 100+ Tech Giants Warn Governments: AI Cyberattacks Are a Real and Urgent Threat
stories.why_it_matters: In an unprecedented joint move, more than 100 companies — including Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic — have signed a statement calling for urgent government action to defend against AI-powered cyberattacks. The concern is that AI tools can now be weaponised to launch far more sophisticated hacking, phishing and disinformation campaigns than ever before. For everyday people, this means the phishing emails and scam calls you already deal with are about to get a whole lot harder to detect. The industry is essentially asking governments to step up before it's too late.

stories.title: Musk, Altman, and Huang to Speak at G20 Tech Meeting
stories.why_it_matters: Elon Musk, Sam Altman (OpenAI) and Jensen Huang (Nvidia) are all confirmed to speak at the upcoming G20 tech summit. This is the first time the world's three most powerful AI figures will appear together at a major intergovernmental forum. The agenda is expected to cover AI governance, global standards, and the economic implications of rapid AI deployment — outcomes from this meeting could shape regulation for years.

stories.title: AI Regulation in Education: Florida Plans Rules from Pre-K to PhD
stories.why_it_matters: Florida's DeSantis administration is pushing to become the first US state to regulate AI use across the entire education system — from kindergarten all the way through university. The proposed rules would govern how AI tools can be used in classrooms, assessments and research. This is part of a growing global push to set guardrails on AI in schools before it fundamentally changes how kids learn and how cheating works. Australia's own education ministers are watching closely.

stories.title: The Regulation Gap: AI-Powered Influence Operations Flying Under the Radar
stories.why_it_matters: A new analysis highlights a major legal blind spot: AI is already being used to run influence operations — fake social media accounts, generated news articles, synthetic voices — and there are almost no specific laws to stop it. Existing rules on disinformation and propaganda weren't written with AI-generated content in mind, meaning political actors can use AI to manipulate public opinion with near-zero legal risk. This is increasingly relevant with multiple major elections coming up globally, including the US midterms.

sport.summary: Storm demolished the Broncos 46-20 at Suncorp last night in a brutal Round 26 opener. The Sea Eagles and Dragons are currently in a first-half battle at 4-0. Finals fever is building across NRL and AFL, with big injury and transfer news to boot.

stories.title: Storm Demolish Broncos 46-20 at Suncorp — Cameron Munster Fires
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Storm put on a masterclass at Suncorp Stadium last night, thrashing the home-side Broncos 46-20 in Round 26. Cameron Munster was prominent and used the game to publicly put the boot into the NRL's new kick-off rule, though the numbers suggest it didn't stop his team from running riot. This was a statement performance from Storm heading into finals, and a worrying result for the Broncos on their own patch.

stories.title: Devastating Finals Injury — Star Fullback Racing the Clock
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports reports a 'devastating' injury on the eve of finals to a star fullback, who is now racing the clock to be fit. The article doesn't name the player explicitly in the available data, but the timing — heading into the business end of the season — makes this a significant story. Check the Fox Sports link for the full player details. Big implications for finals betting and team selection.

stories.title: Bulldogs Hit by Illness Ahead of Panthers Clash Tonight
stories.why_it_matters: The Bulldogs are battling illness in their squad ahead of tonight's 8pm clash against Penrith Panthers at CommBank Stadium. A sickness bug running through the team ahead of such a big game adds real uncertainty to the result. Panthers are chasing a strong finish to the regular season, while the Bulldogs will be severely tested if they're missing key players.

stories.title: Panthers Lose Unsung Hero to Bulldogs for 2027
stories.why_it_matters: Penrith Panthers fans have received some unwelcome news: an unsung hero has confirmed he's signed with the Canterbury Bulldogs for the 2027 season. While he may not be a household name, these kinds of depth departures can quietly hurt premiership contenders who rely on squad depth. The Bulldogs continue their aggressive recruitment rebuild under their new direction.

stories.title: AFL Finals: Every Team's Case — and Blues Reality Laid Bare
stories.why_it_matters: With AFL finals just around the corner, Fox Sports has broken down the case for and against all 10 finalists winning the flag — and the news isn't great for Carlton. Despite a promising year, the Blues' path to a premiership has been exposed as extremely narrow given their form and draw. It's must-read content for any footy fan with finals tips on the line.
